inspection_comments: No violations observed at time of inspection. Observed an employee wearing gloves to prevent bare hand contact while washing and slicing ready to eat food items such as broccoli floret. Discussed the importance of washing hands between gloves changes and after any source of contamination such as eating, drinking, coughing, sneezing, using the restroom or returning to food service after any kind of break. Employees had also pre-packaged ready to eat food items such as strawberries and apples in plastic bags so that bare hand contact can be avoided when students take the food item off of the service line. Multiple digital probe thermometers were available to ensure that potentially hazardous food items (PHF) such as cooked carrots are cooked to 140F or above. Temperatures for hot holding, cold holding and cooking of PHF items served that day were recorded on log sheets. Observed required cold holding temperatures (45F or below) of PHF such as honeydew melon slices in the double door refrigeration unit behind the service line (actual 38F). Observed required hot holding temperatures (140F or above) of PHF such as commercially pre-cooked chicken nuggets in the hot holding cabinet behind the service line (actual 148F). Facility had just received an order of food product and were actively working to store food items in cold holding or dry storage. Discussed that ready to eat food items such as bread and raw produce should be stored on the highest shelving followed by PHF items according to minimum required cooking temperatures with foods requiring the highest minimum cooking temperatures stored on bottom shelving to prevent against possible cross contamination. Test strips were available to ensure that quaternary ammonia sanitizing solution is at a strength of at least 200ppm for sanitizing both dishes/utensils and food contact surfaces.
